title: Please fix linux paths
body:
Currently, for sound files it uses:
```
audioPath = QCoreApplication::applicationDirPath() + "/sounds/"
```

which unfortunately is set on multiple places. On Linux (or at least in Fedora) it's installed the following way:

Binaries:
```
/usr/bin/EchoCallSim
/usr/bin/cablog
/usr/bin/echosim
/usr/bin/fcal
/usr/bin/fmeasure
/usr/bin/fmtave
/usr/bin/fst4sim
/usr/bin/ft8code
/usr/bin/ft8sim
/usr/bin/hash22calc
/usr/bin/jt4code
/usr/bin/jt65code
/usr/bin/jt9
/usr/bin/jt9code
/usr/bin/message_aggregator
/usr/bin/msk144code
/usr/bin/q65code
/usr/bin/q65sim
/usr/bin/testEchoCall
/usr/bin/udp_daemon
/usr/bin/wsjtx
/usr/bin/wsjtx_app_version
/usr/bin/wsprd
```

Arch independent files:
```
/usr/share/wsjtx/ALLCALL7.TXT
/usr/share/wsjtx/JPLEPH
/usr/share/wsjtx/cty.dat
/usr/share/wsjtx/cty.dat_copyright.txt
/usr/share/wsjtx/eclipse.txt
/usr/share/wsjtx/grid.dat
/usr/share/wsjtx/sat.dat
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/CQ.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/CQZone.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/CQZoneOnBand.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/Continent.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/ContinentOnBand.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/DXCC.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/DXCCOnBand.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/DXcall.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/Grid.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/GridOnBand.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/ITUZone.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/ITUZoneOnBand.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/Message.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/MyCall.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/Testing_long.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/_Testing.wav
/usr/share/wsjtx/sounds/_Zone.wav
```

Unfortunately, the `applicationDirPath()` returns the executable path, in such case the `/usr/bin`. Also the `ALLCALL7.TXT` is searched in the `/usr/bin/` in this case.

On linux we cannot put everything in the `/usr/share/wsjtx` and symlink the binaries from the `/usr/bin/` because `/usr/share` is arch independent. Similarly, the `/usr/bin` or `/usr/libexec` are arch dependent.

It would be great if these paths could be set in the cmake without downstream patching.

title: HOUND mode delay when click on call sign
body:
This may or may not be part of the intended design of FT8
standard HOUND mode. I.e. I don't know if it is a bug. It isn't
serious though.  WSJT-X 3.0.1-GA. Discovery on 5/17/26. This
HOUND mode testing was done on 20m when no FOX was operating.

With HOUND deselected I can at any time click on any TX-side
call in the Band Activity window and it will set up the Generate
Std Msgs table ready to QSO with him. But immediately (a few
seconds) after HOUND mode is enabled, depending on the timing
(odd or even cycle), such clicks are ignored.  A few seconds
later another click will do the setup normally. I have been
unable to find time in the past 48 hours to continue testing for
any correlation with odd or even timing shown in Band Activity.
My initial assumption (could be wrong) that initializing HOUND
mode establishes some kind of lockout during that immediate even
cycle.

Software: Windows 10 laptop,  22H2, without use of accessory
software apps like logging software, JTalert, HRD, OmniRig, etc.

title: TCI client: four interoperability issues found implementing a TCI device (WSJT-X 3.0.1)
body:
I am the author of CAT4OM, a multi-radio CAT control system that can present a conventional transceiver to other software as a TCI device. I have just finished getting WSJT-X to work against it with a Yaesu FTDX101D, and it now decodes FT8 through the TCI path as well as it does from a direct sound card.

Getting there took considerably longer than it should have, because on four points the WSJT-X TCI client behaves differently from what the TCI specification describes. I found all four by reading your source rather than from the documentation, which is not a route every implementer will have. None of them is hard to work around once known, so I am reporting them in the hope of saving the next person the same week. Line references are to the 3.0.1 sources.

**1. audio_start / audio_stop must be echoed back, though the specification calls them unidirectional**

Transceiver/TCITransceiver.cpp:457-464 sends audio_start, then blocks for 500 ms waiting for stream_audio_, which is only set when the client receives an audio_start line back from the device (Cmd_AudioStart). If the device does not echo it, WSJT-X reports "TCI Audio could not be switched on" and drops the connection.

The specification classifies both commands as "Unidirectional control ... Sent only by the TCI client", i.e. it states that a device should not send them back. A device that follows the specification here cannot stream audio to WSJT-X at all.

The 500 ms budget is also tight for a device that opens a real audio endpoint on demand: opening a WASAPI capture device on Windows took us ~590 ms, over budget on its own. We now send the echo before opening any device, but a longer timeout, or one that starts after the echo, would be friendlier.

Suggestion: either document the echo as required, or accept a device that does not echo.

**2. length means different things in the two directions**

For RX_AUDIO_STREAM, length is the total number of floats in the payload — frames × channels. This is clear from the header comment (TCITransceiver.hpp:31, "data field length number of float numbers") and from writeAudioData(), which uses it directly as the loop bound and derives frames as maxSize / bytesPerFrame.

For TX_CHRONO, the same field is treated as frames: onBinaryReceived sizes the reply buffer as AudioHeaderSize + pStream->length * sizeof(float) * 2 (TCITransceiver.cpp:868).

Both readings are defensible against the specification's own wording ("number of samples"), which does not say which. But a single field with opposite meanings in the two directions is a trap: sending frames on RX makes WSJT-X read exactly half of every stereo packet and discard the rest, which produces audio that looks and measures correct — correct envelope, silence between FT8 slots — and never decodes. That failure mode is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

Suggestion: document the asymmetry explicitly, since changing it now would break existing devices.

**3. TX audio is gated on a vendor name match, not on a capability**
**### That's the thing that is creating actual issues to my implementation**

TCITransceiver.cpp:1083-1089 has two forms of the PTT command:

if (ESDR3) cmd = CmdTrx + ":" + rx_ + "," + (on?"true":"false") + "," + "tci" + ";";
else       cmd = CmdTrx + ":" + rx_ + "," + (on?"true":"false") + ";";
ESDR3 is set in exactly one place, by exact string comparison on the identity the device announces (TCITransceiver.cpp:818):

case Cmd_Version:
  if(args.at(0)=="ExpertSDR3") ESDR3 = true;
  else if (args.at(0)=="Thetis") HPSDR = true;
A device that announces itself honestly — ours says protocol:CAT4OM,2.0; — therefore never receives the tci audio-source argument, and a device that requires it will transmit silence indefinitely. The symptom is unhelpful: PTT works, the radio keys, and nothing indicates why no audio was requested.

The same flag also selects rx_sensors_enable / tx_sensors_enable over rx_smeter, so it governs several unrelated behaviours at once.

The practical effect is that a third-party TCI device has to choose between announcing its real identity and getting the full feature set. We chose to keep our identity and accept the key-down edge alone as the signal to send TX audio; impersonating ExpertSDR3 would have worked, but it would tie us to another product's version history and would also switch the S-meter path away from one we had already verified.

Suggestion: gate these on a capability the device advertises rather than on its name — the protocol already has a capability exchange. Failing that, sending the tci argument unconditionally would be harmless for devices that ignore a third argument they do not expect.

**4. channel_count vs channels_count**

WSJT-X matches the key channels_count (plural). The specification §4.1 writes CHANNEL_COUNT (singular). A device following the specification is silently treated as having no channel information. We emit both spellings, which costs nothing, but the mismatch is worth fixing on one side or the other.

For completeness, one problem in this exercise was entirely ours: we briefly concluded from m_amp = std::numeric_limits<qint16>::max() that the wire carried int16-scale floats. store() and load() make it plain that ±1.0 is correct in both directions, and we were wrong. I mention it only so the list above is not read as four complaints where one of our own belongs.

I am happy to test patches against real hardware — we have an FTDX101D on this side and the TCI device implementation is ours, so both ends can be instrumented.

Thanks for WSJT-X, and for keeping it open enough that all of the above was findable at all.

Best regards, Daniele Pistollato

title: WSPR "enable tx" and tx% timer not working (3.0.2)
body:
Enabling the "Enable tx" button (highlights red) in WSPR mode does not reliably start tx cycles. WSPR will start a tx cycle, and then will not perform any more (tx is not being triggered at the beginning of a cycle), irrespective of the tx% value. Sometimes clicking "tx next" (highlights red) will force an initial tx cycle at the beginning of the next timeslot, but no more will occur.

Sometimes having tx% at 100% will cause tx every cycle (as expected)

3.0.2
Windows 10
deleted and auto created the wsjtx.ini file - issue still present
restarted app many times
TUNE succesfully causes a tx with tune tone
no tx watchdog enabled
no swr inhibit enabled
pc clock controlled by NTP client and up to date
FT8 / FST4W seem to work ok.
After switching into FT8 and back to WSPR, tx cycle appears to be triggered succesfully.
